newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BONDS DEALT DOUBLE BLOW BY U.S.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BONDS DEALT DOUBLE BLOW BY U.S.

text.p: *An initial mark-up in Australian bond yields after Friday's massive sell-off in U.S. Treasuries turned more aggressive in afternoon trading as U.S. hedge funds sold futures heavily.
An initial mark-up in Australian bond yields after Friday's massive sell-off in U.S. Treasuries turned more aggressive in afternoon trading as U.S. hedge funds sold futures heavily.

Tentative buying going into the lunchtime recess proved shortlived as key support at 93.230 on the local 10-year bond futures contract caved in, adding to the string of major levels broken in the last couple of days.
"The offshore does seem to be a bit more aggressive selling the market. They have the other negative of currency risk," one trader said.
The local dollar put in a modest recovery on Monday after sinking to a two-year low below US$0.7300 late last week.
Until today, domestic debt had been holding up reasonably well against the backdrop of a weakening U.S. Treasury market, largely based on Australia's superior fundamental outlook.

"The U.S. Treasury market looks precariously balanced and the Australian bond market cannot escape a mark-up in yields on Treasury market weakness, even though the local economy is at a different stage of the cycle," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
"Australian fundamentals suggest little reason why local bond yields need to back-up particularly far in the near term," Roberts added.

However, souring technicals appear to be overshadowing fundamentals for now after recoiling from the record peak on the 10-year bond of 93.695 set on August 1, and the market is at risk to a further sell-off if the U.S. remains under pressure.

The U.S. market remains gripped over concerns of economic expansion, and while there are no major indicators due out on Monday, the data flow picks up mid-week with July PPI and retail sales due on Wednesday, and CPI on Thursday.

Local bond yield spreads blew out sharply against the dollar bloc, particularly against Canada which outperformed the U.S. on Friday. The local yield steepened with the impact of the U.S. sell-off having a larger impact on the long end.
